subject: Pilot performance gating & acceptance checklist (MAP)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Rivers <jamie.rivers@peregrinelabs.com>; contracts@peregrinelabs.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot performance gating & acceptance checklist (MAP)

Jamie — following our call this morning, attached is the first draft of the performance section we'll include in the Mutual Action Plan. This note outlines the scope, workload slices, success criteria and the proposed run cadence so we can align on go/no-go gates before pilot close. High-level items: 

- Workload definition (attached): three slices — convo_chat (avg 125 tokens/request), summarization (avg 350 tokens), and embeddings (batch size 64).
- Concurrency targets: steady-state 40 concurrent end-user sessions; spike test at 80 concurrent sessions for 10 minutes.
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) targets: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 320ms for convo_chat under steady-state.
- Latency for full-generation: p50 <= 400ms, p95 <= 900ms (depends on model variant).
- Throughput baseline: target >= 2,000 tokens/sec aggregated across the pool for mixed workload.
- Success criteria: all steady-state SLOs met in 3 of 3 run windows; no more than 5% request retry rate; no functional regressions per the evaluation prompts.

Planned run windows: three 2-hour windows over one week (detailed dates in attachment). We'll collect KV-cache hit-rate, batching efficiency, and TTFT distributions. Deliverables: run results CSV, trimmed trace artifacts, and an acceptance recommendation.

Attachments: MAP_performance_plan_v1.xlsx (workload slices, env config), workload_profiles.csv (samples), run-results-template.csv

Next steps: Please confirm the steady-state concurrency target and whether you want an additional "low-latency" slice (single-turn queries, 1-2 tokens output) included. Once confirmed we'll lock the run schedule and instrument the workload harness.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jamie Rivers <jamie.rivers@peregrinelabs.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot performance gating & acceptance checklist (MAP)

Marissa — quick review notes from infra/serving side. Couple of clarifying asks before we lock the plan: 

1) Model variants: which model family/version will you be validating (fp16 baseline vs 4-bit quant)? We should run both if Peregrine wants the cost/latency tradeoff documented.
2) Baseline environment: confirm whether the pilot runs on Dedicated pool (redwood-dedicated-us-west) or Hosted; affects cache locality and expected TTFT.
3) Cold-start behavior: we need an explicit cold-cache pass (30 minutes idle) and a warmed pass. TTFT SLOs should be split by cold vs warmed.
4) Spike test: suggest a 2x spike for 15 minutes and an additional soak at 1.5x for 60 minutes to validate autoscale behavior.

Proposed tweak to success criteria: require steady-state SLOs met in 2 of 3 windows, plus passing the cold-start and spike windows (no catastrophic errors). Also recommend we capture a small sample of user prompt sets for quality regression checks — if latency optimization increases hallucination rate we need to catch it.

Jonas
Principal Performance Engineer

From: Jamie Rivers <jamie.rivers@peregrinelabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot performance gating & acceptance checklist (MAP)

Thanks Marissa — this looks thorough and aligned with what Peregrine needs. A few questions from my side: 

- We definitely want both the fp16 and 4-bit quant runs. Please include cost estimates for each run in the final MAP doc so procurement can budget.
- Run windows: can we schedule them next week (Jan 19/20/21) mornings PST?
- Go/no-go: please confirm the pass/fail logic in plain language. For example: if p95 TTFT exceeds 400ms in more than one steady-state window, is that an automatic no-go or is there a remediation window?

Also cc'ing contracts; they'll need the MAP as an appendix to the SOW.

Jamie Rivers
Head of ML Ops, Peregrine Labs
jamie.rivers@peregrinelabs.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Rivers <jamie.rivers@peregrinelabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot performance gating & acceptance checklist (MAP)

Jamie — answered inline below and updated acceptance language. Plain-language pass/fail (proposed):

- Steady-state criteria: All steady-state SLOs (TTFT p50/p95, latency p95, throughput >= target) must be met in at least 2 of 3 scheduled run windows.
- Cold-start criteria: Cold cache run must not show p95 TTFT > 600ms.
- Spike criteria: Spike window (2x concurrency) may see degraded perf, but no more than 5% increase in request error rate and no model OOMs.
- Remediation window: If a steady-state SLO fails in 2 of 3 windows, Redwood and Peregrine get a 48-hour remediation period to tune batching/pinning/quant settings and re-run one additional validation window. Final decision (go/no-go) after remediation will be based on the combined outcomes of original and remediation runs.

Schedule: proposed runs Jan 19 (warm), Jan 20 (cold), Jan 21 (spike) all 9:00–11:00 PST. I'll coordinate infra and send the run commands and instrumentation checklist by EOD Friday.

Attachments: run-results-template.csv (pre-populated example rows)

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jamie — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming the schedule and acceptance flow below (locking dates):

- Run windows: Jan 19 (warm), Jan 20 (cold), Jan 21 (spike) 09:00–11:00 PST.
- Model variants: fp16 baseline + 4-bit quantized. We'll include a short cost estimate in the MAP appendix.
- Pass/fail: adopt Rishi's language; remediation window 48 hours if steady-state criteria not met.
- Deliverables to Peregrine within 48 hours of last run: populated run-results CSV, a 2-page summary of SLO outcomes, and a recommendation (GO / CONDITIONAL GO / NO GO).

I've added the finalized acceptance wording to the MAP draft and uploaded a new file to the HubSpot deal (link below). Contracts — please use the attached MAP excerpt as an appendix for the SOW.
